## Overview

**In plain terms.** Among the children who scored zero on phonetic spelling at the start
of the study, *when* did they first come off that floor, and what predicted it? Rather than
the single first-window off-floor transition (the LRPITT09 floor rule), this model uses all
four waves: a discrete-time survival model for the time to first come off the phonetic-
spelling floor, with the intervention entering as a shift in the hazard of coming off.

**Estimand and design.** The at-risk set is the children at the phonetic-spelling floor at
t1. The outcome is the interval (t1→t2, t2→t3, t3→t4) in which a child first scores above
zero. The hazard carries a per-interval baseline, the *baseline* (t1) letter-sound knowledge,
word reading and age as prognostic covariates, and a treatment hazard contrast fitted **in
the randomised first interval only**: after the waitlist crossover every person-period row is
treatment-on, so the later intervals carry no arm contrast and fit their own
(both-arms-treated) baseline hazards. `G = 2 − group`, so a positive `tau` means the
intervention arm has the higher first-interval off-floor hazard.

**What `tau` is.** A model-based, available-case modified-ITT assignment contrast: the
covariate-adjusted immediate-versus-waitlist off-floor hazard contrast in the randomised
first interval among children at the floor at t1 (a pre-randomisation subgroup). The
subgroup restriction, the observed-wave-2 requirement, mean-imputed baseline covariates and
the hazard-model form qualify it, and this family releases no causal headline.
Unlike nonword reading, phonetic spelling's first-window off-floor signal does not replicate
cleanly at the waitlist crossover (see the descriptive note), so the treatment contrast here
is expected to be weak and uncertain. Read the covariate ordering, not the treatment
magnitude.

## Model

With interval baseline hazard $\alpha_k$, treatment-on indicator $\text{trt}_{ik}$, and
standardised baseline covariates $L_{0,i}$ (letter sounds), $W_{0,i}$ (word reading) and
$A_{0,i}$ (age), the discrete-time hazard of coming off the floor uses a
complementary-log-log link:

$$
\text{cloglog}\big(h_{ik}\big) = \alpha_k + \tau\,\text{trt}_{ik}\,[k = 1]
  + \beta_L\,L_{0,i} + \beta_W\,W_{0,i} + \beta_A\,A_{0,i},
\qquad [\,\text{off floor in interval } k\,]_{ik} \sim \text{Bernoulli}(h_{ik}).
$$

The $[k = 1]$ indicator restricts `tau` to the randomised first interval
(`treatment_window="randomised"`, 2026-08-21 survival review): the legacy pooled shift
across all intervals had no likelihood contrast beyond interval 1 and its direction was
prior-mediated; it remains available as the explicit `treatment_window="pooled"` comparator.
A logistic-hazard link is the documented sensitivity variant.
